co_overlook_the.blurb: The Overlook is a small upper-tier cliff in Boulder Canyon, perched at roughly 7,900 feet above the creek and reached by a short walk past Broken Rock. It holds 19 climbs: mostly trad, with a handful of sport lines and three boulder problems. Routes are generally single pitches of about 45 to 80 feet that follow cracks, flakes, corners and roofs, with some steep faces. Grades run from the high 5.7s up to 5.13, with the bulk of the roped climbs sitting around 5.11, so it suits strong leaders more than beginners. It is a quiet spot with big views, and being on the canyon's south side it sees little winter sun and works better in warm weather.

co_05_thunder_tactics.blurb: Thunder Tactics is the fifth wall along the north side of The Bank at Shelf Road, near Canon City, sitting between Dave Dangle and Surreal Estate. It is almost entirely sport climbing: 18 bolted lines plus a single trad route. Most of the 19 climbs fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a few 5.9s and 5.8s to start on and a couple of 5.12s at the top end. Its namesake 5.11c is a classic that begins from a ledge about 30 feet up. This part of The Bank is among the busier stretches of the canyon, and the north-side walls here tend to get morning shade.

co_east_ridge_3.blurb: East Ridge is a two-step spine in Fern Canyon, in the southern Flatirons of Boulder, wedged between Goose Ridge and Nebel Horn Ridge. The lower step is the Fiddlehead, while the upper step has a slab with many sport lines and dihedrals better suited to trad. Of the 19 climbs, most are trad with a few sport routes, and grades run from easy fourth-class terrain to 5.12, with 5.11 the most common. Faces on the ridge point south, which makes it a good bet on sunny days outside the heat of summer. Plan on a long approach of well over an hour along the Fern Canyon trail, with some scrambling to reach the upper dihedrals.
co_east_ridge_3.approach: Follow the Fern Canyon trail past the big Superfresh block, then either take a faint path up the gully beside the Fiddlehead or continue to the ridge top and bushwhack along the crest. Class 3 scrambling leads to the upper dihedrals.
